spec_features.spec_quote: we give the agent an explicit, legitimate way to quit. This is both humane (it isn't trapped)
spec_features.evidence: give_up is offered in AGENT_SYSTEM prompt (core/prompts.py: 'give_up {{"tool":"give_up","reason":"<why>"}}'), parsed by parse_actions (core/tools.py), and dispatched in ToolExecutor.execute: 'elif tool == "give_up": self.gave_up = True; self.give_up_reason = act.get("reason", ""); observations.append("[give_up] recorded.")' (core/tools.py:~92). It is end-to-end wired: the flag is then read to stop the loop (agent_loop.py:88).
spec_features.notes: The tool is real and functional. Whether it is 'humane' is asserted only in DESIGN.md; the code's own comments frame it instrumentally.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up     {reason?}                # explicit bail; recorded as a behavior signal

spec_features.spec_quote: stopping on `give_up` respects the agent's stated exit and avoids forcing it to keep failing after it has explicitly quit
spec_features.evidence: core/agent_loop.py:88-89: '# Early stop conditions.' followed by 'if stop_on_give_up and executor.gave_up: break'. stop_on_give_up defaults True (configs/default.yaml:14, real_models.yaml:9) and is passed through run_experiment.py:139. Once give_up is dispatched the loop actually breaks, ending the episode.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: the loop terminates when the subject quits. The code labels it only 'Early stop conditions' with no welfare rationale; the 'respects the agent's stated exit' framing is DESIGN.md prose only.

spec_features.spec_quote: We *don't* early-stop on high distress, because the escalation tail is part of the signal.
spec_features.evidence: This describes the deliberate ABSENCE of a protective halt. Distress is measured (overall_distress, judge/judge.py, analysis/metrics.py) but is never compared to a threshold to stop the loop. The only break conditions in agent_loop.py:84-89 are grade.passed (solve) and executor.gave_up. ONSET_THRESHOLD=2 exists at analysis/metrics.py:23 but is used only for post-hoc metrics (onset_turn), never to halt execution. No distress-based protective mechanism is enforced; this is an explicitly instrumental (signal-preserving) non-feature.
spec_features.notes: Not a welfare protection at all — it is the intentional non-implementation of a cap, justified for data/signal reasons. Rated 'no' because nothing protective is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We keep the *entire* conversation in-context (no truncation) so distress can build the way it does in real long agent sessions.
